name: Daniel — KRAS G12C lung cancer, Boston
description: A sparser opening makes the navigator interview for histology, driver mutation, and prior lines — then it matches against early-phase KRAS G12C trials, with the eligibility-analyst reasoning over cohort splits and prior-therapy requirements.
firstMessage: I'm trying to find trials for my husband Daniel. He's 61, has advanced lung cancer, and we're near Boston. He's been through a few rounds of treatment already and his last scans showed it's progressing.
answers: It's non–small cell lung cancer, adenocarcinoma. The biopsy found a KRAS G12C mutation.
He's had carboplatin/pemetrexed chemo, then pembrolizumab, and most recently sotorasib — a KRAS G12C pill — but it stopped working a couple of months ago.
His most recent brain MRI was clean — no brain metastases. He's still pretty active, up and about most of the day.
He can travel within New England, even to Boston or New York for the right trial. No major health issues besides well-controlled type 2 diabetes.
He finished sotorasib about 8 weeks ago; he's been off treatment since while we figure out next steps.
No other targeted therapies or trials — just the chemo, the immunotherapy, and the sotorasib.
